0: Calmly and gracefully thou movest along the path of life, tearless and smileless, and scarce a heedless glance of indifferent attention ruffles thy calm.
1: Thou art good and wise ... and all things are remote from thee, and of no one hast thou need.
2: Thou art fair, and no one can say, whether thou prizest thy beauty or not. No sympathy hast thou to give; none dost thou desire.
3: Thy glance is deep, and no thought is in it; in that clear depth is emptiness.
4: So in the Elysian field, to the solemn strains of Gluck’s melodies, move without grief or bliss the graceful shades.
